question: Which of the following players is associated with boxing?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lovlina Borgohain.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lovlina Borgohain is an Indian boxer from Assam who competes in the welterweight (69 kg) category. (मुक्केबाज — लवलीना बोरगोहेन)

 

• She won the bronze medal in boxing at the Tokyo Olympics 2020, becoming only the third Indian boxer, after Vijender Singh (2008) and M.C. Mary Kom (2012), to win an Olympic medal.

 

• She trains at the National Boxing Academy and hails from Golaghat district, Assam; she was earlier a kickboxer before switching to boxing.

 

• She was honoured with the Khel Ratna Award (Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna) and the Padma Shri for her achievements.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mary Kom and Vijender Singh are the other two Indian boxers to have won Olympic medals, in 2012 (London) and 2008 (Beijing) respectively.

 

NOTE

 

• Archana Kamat (Option 1): She is an Indian table tennis player.

 

• Hima Das (Option 3): Known as the "Dhing Express", she is an Indian track and field sprinter (400 m).

 

• Monica Batra (Option 4): Not associated with boxing; included as a distractor.

question: Who among the following Indian music directors won the Best Original Score at Amsterdam International Film Festival in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ilaiyaraaja.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Legendary composer Ilaiyaraaja, popularly known as "Isaignani" (musical genius), won the Best Original Score award at the Amsterdam International Film Festival (AIFF) 2022. (इलैयाराजा — सर्वश्रेष्ठ मूल स्कोर पुरस्कार)

 

• The award recognised his background score for the Tamil film "A Beautiful Breakup", released in early 2022.

 

• Ilaiyaraaja has composed music for over 1,000 films across South Indian and Hindi cinema and is regarded as one of the greatest film composers in Indian history.

 

• He was conferred the Padma Bhushan (2018) and the Padma Vibhushan (2024) by the Government of India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ilaiyaraaja is also known for pioneering the use of Western classical orchestration blended with Indian folk and Carnatic music in Tamil film scores.

 

NOTE

 

• A.R. Rahman (Option 1): An internationally acclaimed composer and two-time Academy Award (Oscar) winner for Slumdog Millionaire (2008), but he did not win this particular AIFF 2022 award.

 

• Santosh Narayanan (Option 2): A Tamil film composer known for films like Jigarthanda and Sarpatta Parambarai; not the AIFF 2022 winner.

 

• Harris Jayaraj (Option 3): A well-known Tamil film composer, associated with several Tamil and Telugu hit soundtracks; not the AIFF 2022 winner.

question: In 2015, the Planning Commission was replaced with the ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is NITI Aayog.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Planning Commission, established in 1950, was replaced by the NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) on 1 January 2015. (नीति आयोग — योजना आयोग का स्थान)

 

• NITI Aayog serves as the premier policy think tank of the Government of India, providing directional and strategic input, in contrast to the Planning Commission's top-down, resource-allocating role.

 

• The Prime Minister is the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog, and it has a Vice-Chairperson appointed by the PM.

 

• Unlike the Planning Commission, NITI Aayog does not have the power to impose five-year plans on states or allocate central funds to ministries/states.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog was Arvind Panagariya.

 

• NITI Aayog's Governing Council includes all state Chief Ministers and Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories, promoting cooperative federalism.

 

NOTE

 

• Monetary Policy Committee (Option 1): A body under the RBI that decides the benchmark policy interest rate (repo rate).

 

• Competition Commission of India (Option 2): A statutory body that enforces the Competition Act, 2002 to prevent anti-competitive practices.

 

• NaBFID (Option 3): The National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development, set up in 2021 to fund long-term infrastructure projects.

question: Which of the following is an organic compound with the formula CH3OC6H5 used as a perfume, fragrance and solvent?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anisole.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Anisole (methoxybenzene), with the formula CH3OC6H5, is an aromatic ether formed by a methyl group bonded to the oxygen of a phenol. (एनीसोल — इत्र/सुगंध द्रव्य)

 

• It has a pleasant, sweet, anise-like odour and is widely used as an intermediate in perfume and fragrance manufacturing, and as a solvent.

 

• It is also used as a starting material for organic synthesis, including the synthesis of certain pharmaceuticals and pesticides.

 

• Anisole is a colourless liquid, derived structurally by replacing the hydrogen of phenol's –OH group with a methyl group.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Anisole undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution readily because the methoxy group is an ortho/para-directing, activating group.

 

NOTE

 

• Toluene (Option 2): Formula C6H5CH3; an aromatic hydrocarbon used as an industrial solvent and in fuel additives.

 

• Acetophenone (Option 3): Formula C6H5COCH3; an aromatic ketone with a sweet, almond-like smell used in fragrances.

 

• Aniline (Option 4): Formula C6H5NH2; an aromatic amine used mainly in the dye and rubber industries.

question: ______ in a particular direction is velocity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Speed.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Velocity is defined as speed in a particular (specified) direction — it is the rate of change of displacement with respect to time. (वेग — दिशा में चाल)

 

• Velocity is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction, whereas speed is a scalar quantity, having only magnitude.

 

• The SI unit of both speed and velocity is metre per second (m/s).

 

• When the direction of motion does not change, the magnitude of velocity equals speed; when direction changes (e.g., circular motion), velocity can change even if speed is constant.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time and is also a vector quantity, measured in m/s².

 

• Average velocity = total displacement / total time, while average speed = total distance / total time.

 

NOTE

 

• Acceleration (Option 1): This describes the rate of change of velocity, not velocity itself.

 

• Displacement (Option 2): This is the change in position (a vector), not "speed in a direction" — velocity is the rate of change of displacement.

 

• Distance (Option 4): This is a scalar quantity denoting total path length covered, unrelated to direction.

question: Birju Maharaj was awarded which of the following awards in 2012?
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Film Award.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Birju Maharaj, the doyen of the Kathak dance form and a member of the Kalka-Bindadin gharana of Lucknow, won the National Film Award for Best Choreography in 2012 for his choreography in the film "Vishwaroopam". (बिरजू महाराज — कथक, राष्ट्रीय फिल्म पुरस्कार)

 

• He was a torchbearer of the Lucknow Kathak Gharana, and was celebrated equally as a dancer, choreographer, singer, and percussionist.

 

• Earlier in his career, he had also choreographed for acclaimed films such as "Devdas" (2002) and "Dedh Ishqiya", among others.

 

• He received India's civilian honours — the Padma Vibhushan (1986) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1964) — much earlier in his career, distinct from this 2012 film award.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pandit Birju Maharaj passed away in January 2022; he is remembered as one of India's greatest classical dance gurus.

 

• He also received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (Akademi Ratna), the Akademi's highest honour.

 

NOTE

 

• Sangam Kala Award (Option 1): Not the award received by Birju Maharaj in 2012; it is a distractor.

 

• Filmfare Award (Option 2): A separate private film industry award; not the one he won in 2012.

 

• Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (Option 4): He had already received this award decades earlier, in 1964, not in 2012.

question: Which of the following is commonly known as Quicklime?
solution_text:
The correct answer is CaO.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Calcium oxide (CaO) is commonly known as "Quicklime" or "burnt lime". (चूना/बिना बुझा चूना — CaO)

 

• It is produced industrially by heating (calcining) limestone (CaCO3) at high temperature, releasing carbon dioxide: CaCO3 → CaO + CO2.

 

• Quicklime reacts vigorously and exothermically with water to form calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)2, commonly called slaked lime.

 

• It is used widely in the manufacture of cement, in the steel industry as a flux, and in water and soil treatment.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• A solution of slaked lime in water is called limewater, used to test for the presence of CO2 gas (turns milky).

 

• A mixture of slaked lime, sand and water forms mortar, traditionally used in construction/whitewashing.

 

NOTE

 

• CaSO4 (Option 1): Calcium sulphate; its hemihydrate form is known as Plaster of Paris.

 

• CaCl2 (Option 2): Calcium chloride; commonly used as a drying/desiccating agent and for de-icing roads.

 

• Ca(OH)2 (Option 3): Calcium hydroxide, known as slaked lime, is formed when quicklime reacts with water — it is not quicklime itself.

question: Which road plan in India was the first attempt for the Road Development Programme between 1943-1963?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagpur Road Plan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Nagpur Road Plan (1943-1963) was India's first 20-year road development plan, formulated at a conference of chief engineers held at Nagpur in 1943. (नागपुर रोड योजना — प्रथम सड़क विकास योजना)

 

• Its objective was to build a road system to meet the needs of agriculture, industry and defence in a planned and coordinated manner across the country.

 

• The plan introduced a functional classification of roads into National Highways, State Highways, District Roads, and Village Roads.

 

• It targeted a road density of roughly 16 km of road per 100 sq. km of area, though actual achievement fell short of the target.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Subsequent plans include the Bombay Road Plan (1961-1981), the Lucknow Road Plan (1981-2001), and the Road Development Plan Vision 2021.

 

• The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) was set up in 1988 to manage the National Highways network.

 

NOTE

 

• Poona Road Plan (Option 1): Not a recognised historical road development plan of India; a distractor.

 

• Bombay Road Plan (Option 3): This was the second 20-year road plan (1961-1981), following the Nagpur Plan, not the first.

 

• Lucknow Road Plan (Option 4): This was the third 20-year road plan (1981-2001), not the first.

question: In August 2022, the “SMILE-75 Initiative” was launched by Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment. What is the objective of this scheme?
option_1: To provide education and training to the weaker sections of the society
option_2: To improve immunisation coverage for children and pregnant women in India
option_3: To accelerate the development of biopharmaceuticals
option_4: To make our cities/town and municipal areas begging-free.
solution_text:
The correct answer is To make our cities/town and municipal areas begging-free.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The "SMILE-75" initiative (Support for Marginalised Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise) was launched in August 2022 by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. (स्माइल-75 — भिक्षावृत्ति मुक्त शहर)

 

• Its objective is to make 75 identified cities/towns and municipal areas across India begging-free, through comprehensive rehabilitation of persons engaged in the act of begging.

 

• It focuses on survey, identification, rehabilitation, provision of medical facilities, counselling, education, skill development, and economic linkages for such persons.

 

• The scheme is implemented through a central sector scheme in coordination with State/UT governments, urban local bodies and voluntary/civil society organisations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• SMILE-75 is one of the two sub-schemes under the broader central sector scheme "SMILE: Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise", the other being for the welfare of transgender persons.

 

• It falls under the ambit of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, headed at the time by Dr. Virendra Kumar.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (education/training for weaker sections): Describes a general welfare goal, not the specific objective of SMILE-75.

 

• Option 2 (immunisation coverage): This describes goals of health schemes like Mission Indradhanush, not SMILE-75.

 

• Option 3 (biopharmaceuticals development): This relates to schemes under the Department of Biotechnology, unrelated to SMILE-75.

question: In which year were the 73rd and 74th amendments passed by the Parliament?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1992.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts were passed by the Parliament of India in 1992 and came into force from 24 April 1993 and 1 June 1993 respectively. (73वां व 74वां संशोधन — 1992)

 

• The 73rd Amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs), adding Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution.

 

• The 74th Amendment gave constitutional status to Urban Local Bodies (Municipalities), adding Part IX-A and the Twelfth Schedule.

 

• Both amendments aimed to strengthen grassroots democracy through decentralisation and mandated regular elections via State Election Commissions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 73rd Amendment established a three-tier Panchayati Raj system: Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti (Block), and Zila Parishad (District).

 

• The 74th Amendment created three types of urban bodies: Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council, and Municipal Corporation.

 

NOTE

 

• 1989 (Option 1): This was the year the 61st Amendment (reducing the voting age to 18) was passed, not the 73rd/74th.

 

• 1990 (Option 3): Not the year of passage of these amendments.

 

• 1995 (Option 4): Not the year of passage; the amendments were already in force by 1993.

question: Roshan Kumari is an exponent of which Indian classical dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Roshan Kumari was a renowned exponent of Kathak, belonging to the Jaipur gharana of the dance form. (रोशन कुमारी — कथक नृत्यांगना)

 

• She was trained by the legendary Kathak guru Pandit Sunder Prasad and became one of the leading Kathak dancers of her generation.

 

• She is well known for her performance in Satyajit Ray's classic Bengali film "Jalsaghar" (The Music Room, 1958), where she performed a memorable Kathak sequence.

 

• She was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for her contribution to Kathak.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The three major gharanas (schools) of Kathak are the Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras gharanas.

 

• Other well-known Kathak exponents include Birju Maharaj (Lucknow gharana) and Sitara Devi.

 

NOTE

 

• Odissi (Option 2): A classical dance form of Odisha; noted exponents include Kelucharan Mohapatra and Sonal Mansingh.

 

• Bharatanatyam (Option 3): A classical dance form of Tamil Nadu; noted exponents include Rukmini Devi Arundale.

 

• Kathakali (Option 4): A classical dance-drama form of Kerala, known for elaborate makeup and costumes.

question: Where is the Sair-E-Gul Faroshan festival held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Delhi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sair-e-Gul Faroshan (also known as "Phool Walon Ki Sair", meaning "procession of flower sellers") is a festival held annually in Delhi, particularly in the Mehrauli area. (सैर-ए-गुल फरोशां — दिल्ली)

 

• It was started around 1812 by Mirza Jahangir, son of Mughal emperor Akbar Shah II, as a symbol of gratitude and communal harmony.

 

• The festival involves an offering of a floral chadar (canopy) and pankha (fan) at the Dargah of Khwaja Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki and the nearby Yogmaya Temple, symbolising Hindu-Muslim unity.

 

• It is celebrated over several days, typically in the month of September/October, and is considered a unique example of Delhi's syncretic (Ganga-Jamuni) culture.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The tradition had lapsed for a period after 1942 but was revived in 1962 on the initiative of Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.

 

• The festival is also called the "Festival of Flower Sellers" and features processions, cultural performances, and kite flying.

 

NOTE

 

• Mussoorie (Option 1): A hill station in Uttarakhand, not associated with this festival.

 

• Mumbai (Option 2): Not the location of this festival.

 

• Shimla (Option 4): The capital of Himachal Pradesh, not associated with this festival.

question: Where and when will the fourth edition of the Winter Youth Olympic Games be held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2024 Gangwon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 4th Winter Youth Olympic Games were scheduled to be held in Gangwon, South Korea, in 2024 (held from 19 January to 1 February 2024). (गंगवोन शीतकालीन युवा ओलंपिक 2024)

 

• It was the first Olympic-related event hosted by South Korea since the Pyeongchang 2018 Winter Olympics.

 

• The Winter Youth Olympic Games are held every four years and are organised for athletes aged approximately 14 to 18 years.

 

• Previous editions were held in Innsbruck, Austria (2012), Lillehammer, Norway (2016), and Lausanne, Switzerland (2020).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Summer Youth Olympic Games are a separate, parallel event; Dakar, Senegal was scheduled to host the Summer Youth Olympics (later postponed to 2026).

 

• The Youth Olympic Games concept was proposed by IOC President Jacques Rogge and first held in Singapore (Summer, 2010).

 

NOTE

 

• 2024 Nanjing (Option 1): Nanjing, China hosted the 2014 Summer Youth Olympic Games, not the 2024 Winter edition.

 

• 2026, Dakar (Option 2): Dakar, Senegal was slated to host a Summer Youth Olympic Games, not the Winter edition, and not in the 4th Winter YOG cycle.

 

• 2023 Buenos Aires (Option 3): Buenos Aires hosted the 2018 Summer Youth Olympic Games, not a Winter edition in 2023.

question: According to census 2011, which is the least populous state in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sikkim.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Census 2011, Sikkim is the least populous state in India, with a population of about 6.1 lakh (610,577). (सिक्किम — सबसे कम जनसंख्या वाला राज्य)

 

• Sikkim is also one of the smallest states of India by area and is located in the north-eastern Himalayan region, bordering China, Nepal, and Bhutan.

 

• Its capital is Gangtok, and it became the 22nd state of India in 1975.

 

• Sikkim is notably India's first fully organic farming state.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Among Union Territories (not states), Lakshadweep has the least population as per Census 2011.

 

• Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state in India as per Census 2011.

 

NOTE

 

• Nagaland (Option 1): A north-eastern state with a Census 2011 population greater than Sikkim's (about 19.8 lakh).

 

• Arunachal Pradesh (Option 3): Also a north-eastern state, with a larger population (about 13.8 lakh) than Sikkim.

 

• Goa (Option 4): India's smallest state by area, but its population (about 14.6 lakh) is larger than Sikkim's.

question: Dadabhai Naoroji was a ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Businessman.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dadabhai Naoroji, popularly known as the "Grand Old Man of India", worked as a businessman/merchant — he became a partner in Cama & Co., the first Indian trading firm established in Britain. (दादाभाई नौरोजी — व्यवसायी)

 

• He later founded his own trading firm, Dadabhai Naoroji & Co., in London.

 

• He was also a scholar, professor of mathematics at Elphinstone College, and a prominent political and social leader, being one of the founders of the Indian National Congress (1885) and serving as its President three times (1886, 1893, 1906).

 

• He became the first Indian (Asian) to be elected to the British House of Commons, representing Finsbury Central for the Liberal Party in 1892.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• He propounded the famous "Drain Theory" in his book "Poverty and Un-British Rule in India" (1901), explaining the economic exploitation of India by British colonial rule.

 

• He founded the East India Association (1866) in London to represent Indian interests before the British public.

 

NOTE

 

• Doctor (Option 2): Dadabhai Naoroji was not a medical doctor.

 

• Soldier (Option 3): He had no military career.

 

• British Officer (Option 4): He was an Indian nationalist and critic of British colonial policy, not a British official.

question: Vetti tax that is mentioned in the inscriptions of the Chola dynasty was taken in _____ form.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Forced labour.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vetti, mentioned in Chola dynasty inscriptions, refers to a form of tax collected as unpaid, forced (compulsory) labour rendered to the state or local administration. (वेट्टी कर — बेगार/जबरन श्रम)

 

• It was one of the several local taxes and levies recorded in Chola epigraphs, alongside land-based and produce-based dues.

 

• Villagers were required to render such compulsory services (e.g., for construction, transport, or public works) without wages, as part of their obligations to the state.

 

• The extensive Chola inscriptions, found on temple walls and copper plates, are a major source of information about the administrative and revenue system of the empire, which had a well-organised local self-government structure (Ur, Sabha, Nadu).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Chola administration is particularly noted for its detailed village assemblies (Sabha for Brahmadeya villages), documented via inscriptions like the Uttiramerur inscription.

 

• Land revenue under the Cholas was generally assessed and collected as a share of the produce, distinct from the labour-based vetti.

 

NOTE

 

• Crops (Option 1): This describes produce-based revenue, a separate category of Chola taxation, not vetti.

 

• Land revenue (Option 2): This was a separate, major source of Chola state income, distinct from the labour-tax vetti.

 

• Cash (Option 3): Vetti specifically denotes labour service, not a cash payment.

question: Which of the following statements is correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Water is a cyclic resource.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Water is a cyclic resource, as it continuously moves through the hydrological (water) cycle — evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection — and gets replenished naturally over time. (जल — चक्रीय संसाधन)

 

• Because it cycles and renews itself, water is classified as a renewable natural resource, though its availability in usable form can be limited regionally.

 

• Water exists in three physical states — solid (ice), liquid (water), and gas (water vapour) — depending on temperature and pressure.

 

• As an abiotic (non-living) resource, water is a key component of the natural environment that supports all biotic life but is not itself a living resource.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Natural resources are broadly classified as renewable (e.g., water, solar energy, forests) and non-renewable (e.g., coal, petroleum, minerals).

 

• Other cyclic natural elements include the carbon cycle, nitrogen cycle, and oxygen cycle.

 

NOTE

 

• Water has only one state (Option 2): Incorrect — water exists in three states: solid, liquid, and gas.

 

• Water a non-renewable resource (Option 3): Incorrect — water is renewable, as it is continuously replenished by the water cycle.

 

• Water is a biotic resource (Option 4): Incorrect — water is an abiotic resource, not a living one.

question: The Chinese Buddhist pilgrim, Xuan Zang, came to the Indian subcontinent about _____ years ago.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1400.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Xuan Zang (Hiuen Tsang), a Chinese Buddhist monk and scholar, travelled to the Indian subcontinent during the 7th century CE (around 629-645 CE), roughly 1,400 years ago. (ह्वेनसांग — भारत यात्रा, 7वीं शताब्दी)

 

• He visited India primarily during the reign of King Harshavardhana of Kannauj, and spent considerable time studying Buddhist philosophy at the famed Nalanda University.

 

• On his return to China, he wrote a detailed travelogue titled "Si-Yu-Ki" (Records of the Western World), which is an important historical source for studying India's socio-political and religious conditions during Harsha's reign.

 

• His accounts also describe the flourishing state of Buddhism and Indian society in the early medieval period.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Another notable Chinese pilgrim, Fa-Hien (Faxian), visited India roughly two centuries earlier, during the reign of Chandragupta II of the Gupta dynasty (c. 399-414 CE).

 

• Xuan Zang is often referred to in Indian history as the "Prince of Pilgrims".

 

NOTE

 

• 1100 (Option 1): Understates the time elapsed since Xuan Zang's 7th-century visit.

 

• 1700 (Option 2): Overstates the timeframe; this would place his visit too early, closer to c. 300 CE.

 

• 2000 (Option 3): Significantly overstates the timeframe, corresponding closer to the Mauryan/early historic period.

question: Identify an example of decomposers that are found in the bottom of a pond.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Flagellates.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Flagellates are microorganisms, along with fungi and bacteria, that are especially abundant at the bottom (benthic zone) of a pond, where they act as decomposers, breaking down dead organic matter. (कशाभिक/फ्लैजिलेट्स — तालाब में अपघटक)

 

• Decomposers break down complex organic compounds from dead plants and animals into simpler substances, returning nutrients to the ecosystem.

 

• In a pond ecosystem, the bottom zone (benthos) is where decomposition of settled dead organic matter mainly takes place.

 

• Flagellates possess whip-like structures called flagella used for locomotion, and many species are saprotrophic, feeding on decaying organic material.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• A pond ecosystem is typically divided into zones: littoral (shallow, near shore), limnetic (open water), and benthic (bottom) zones.

 

• Common decomposers across ecosystems include bacteria, fungi, and certain protozoans like flagellates.

 

NOTE

 

• Zooplankton (Option 1): These are small floating/drifting animal organisms, primary/secondary consumers in the food chain, not decomposers.

 

• Jellyfishes (Option 2): These are free-swimming carnivorous animals (consumers), not decomposers, and are not typically found at pond bottoms.

 

• Phytoplankton (Option 4): These are microscopic photosynthetic organisms (producers) found near the water surface, not decomposers.

question: The ___________ is a set of written rules that are accepted by all people living within a country.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Constitution.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Constitution is a set of fundamental, written rules that are accepted by all citizens of a country and that determine the relationship among the people and government institutions. (संविधान — मौलिक लिखित नियम)

 

• The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution in the world, containing a Preamble, Articles, and Schedules, originally adopted on 26 November 1949 and enforced from 26 January 1950.

 

• It serves as the supreme law of the land, laying down the framework for governance, fundamental rights, duties, and the organisation of government institutions.

 

• It was drafted by the Constituent Assembly, chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad, with Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as Chairman of the Drafting Committee.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Constitution can be amended under Article 368, and its basic structure cannot be altered, as held in the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973).

 

• 26 January is celebrated as Republic Day, marking the day the Constitution came into effect.

 

NOTE

 

• Writ (Option 1): A formal written order issued by a court (e.g., Habeas Corpus, Mandamus), not a body of rules for a whole country.

 

• Document (Option 2): A generic term for any written record; too vague to specifically denote the set of governing rules.

 

• Bill (Option 4): A draft proposal of a law placed before the legislature, which becomes an Act only after being passed and receiving assent.

question: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of E-Commerce?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Late response to customer needs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Late response to customer needs" is NOT an advantage of e-commerce — in fact, e-commerce is generally valued for enabling faster, real-time responses to customer needs through online platforms. (ई-कॉमर्स — तीव्र प्रतिक्रिया लाभ)

 

• E-commerce (electronic commerce) refers to the buying and selling of goods and services, and the transfer of funds, over electronic networks such as the internet.

 

• Its recognised advantages include cost saving and price reduction (due to lower overheads), wider choice of products for consumers, improved/faster customer service, 24x7 availability, and wider market reach.

 

• A slow or delayed response to customers is generally considered a disadvantage/limitation of poorly managed e-commerce operations, not a benefit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common types of e-commerce include B2B (Business-to-Business), B2C (Business-to-Consumer), C2C (Consumer-to-Consumer), and C2B.

 

• Challenges of e-commerce include cybersecurity risks, lack of physical inspection of goods, and dependency on internet infrastructure.

 

NOTE

 

• Cost saving and price reduction (Option 1): A genuine, well-recognised advantage of e-commerce due to reduced operational and intermediary costs.

 

• Wider choice (Option 3): A genuine advantage, as e-commerce platforms can showcase a much larger range of products than physical stores.

 

• Improved customer services (Option 4): A genuine advantage, as e-commerce enables features like 24x7 support, tracking, and personalisation.

question: Who has been appointed as the Director General, National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG) in September 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharat Lal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bharat Lal, a retired Indian Forest Service (IFoS) officer of the Gujarat cadre, was appointed as the Director General of the National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG) in September 2022. (भरत लाल — राष्ट्रीय सुशासन केंद्र महानिदेशक)

 

• Prior to this appointment, he served as Additional Secretary in the Ministry of Jal Shakti and was closely associated with the Jal Jeevan Mission.

 

• The NCGG, headquartered in Mussoorie, functions under the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG), Government of India, and works on governance reforms and capacity building of civil servants (including for other countries).

 

• NCGG is registered as an autonomous institution and also conducts training programmes for civil servants from partner nations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bharat Lal was later appointed as a Secretary-General of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC).

 

• NCGG was established in 2014 and evolved from the Indian Institute of Public Administration's Centre for Good Governance initiatives.

 

NOTE

 

• Tarun Kapoor (Option 1): A former IAS officer who served as Secretary in the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas and later as an advisor to the PMO; not the DG NCGG.

 

• Rajiv Bahl (Option 2): Served as Director General of the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), unrelated to NCGG.

 

• Pralay Mondal (Option 3): A banking sector executive, not related to NCGG.

question: Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni was a contemporary of which Chola king?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajendra I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni (ruled Ghazni c. 998-1030 CE) was a contemporary of the Chola king Rajendra I (also known as Rajendra Chola I), who ruled the Chola empire from 1014 to 1044 CE. (महमूद गजनवी — राजेंद्र प्रथम, चोल)

 

• Their reigns overlapped for over a decade (approximately 1014-1030 CE), even though their kingdoms were geographically distant and did not have significant direct conflict.

 

• Rajendra I, son of Rajaraja I, greatly expanded the Chola empire, notably launching a successful naval expedition against the Sri Vijaya empire in Southeast Asia and a campaign to the Gangetic plains, after which he adopted the title "Gangaikonda Chola".

 

• He founded a new capital, Gangaikonda Cholapuram, to commemorate his northern expedition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mahmud of Ghazni is chiefly remembered in Indian history for his repeated raids into India, including the famous raid on the Somnath Temple in Gujarat in 1025 CE.

 

• The Chola dynasty is renowned for its strong navy, extensive maritime trade, and advanced local self-government, as recorded in inscriptions like the Uttiramerur inscription.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajaraja I (Option 1): Ruled from 985-1014 CE, just before Mahmud of Ghazni's major raids into India began around 1000 CE — his reign only marginally overlaps.

 

• Rajendra II (Option 2): Ruled much later, in the mid-11th century (c. 1051-1063 CE), after Mahmud's death in 1030 CE.

 

• Rajadhiraja (Option 3): Ruled from 1044-1054 CE, after Mahmud of Ghazni's death, so they were not contemporaries.

question: In April 2022, which scheme was selected for PM’s Award for Excellence in Public Administration?
solution_text:
The correct answer is UDAN.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik) scheme of the Ministry of Civil Aviation was selected for the Prime Minister's Award for Excellence in Public Administration in April 2022. (उड़ान योजना — सुशासन हेतु प्रधानमंत्री पुरस्कार)

 

• UDAN is a regional connectivity scheme launched in 2016 aimed at making air travel affordable for common citizens and boosting air connectivity to under-served and unserved airports/airstrips.

 

• The award recognised the scheme's contribution to enhancing regional air connectivity and its role in driving inclusive economic growth.

 

• The Prime Minister's Awards for Excellence in Public Administration are conferred annually by the Government of India to recognise exemplary work done by civil servants and government schemes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• UDAN is implemented by Airports Authority of India (AAI), in coordination with State governments and airline/helicopter operators.

 

• The scheme's full form, "Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik", translates to "let the common citizen of the country fly".

 

NOTE

 

• Smile (Option 1): The SMILE scheme relates to rehabilitation of beggars/transgender welfare, launched in 2022, but was not the scheme selected for this particular April 2022 award.

 

• Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (Option 2): A scheme for the welfare of the girl child, launched in 2015, but not the one selected for this award.

 

• Make in India (Option 4): A manufacturing-promotion initiative launched in 2014, not the scheme awarded in April 2022.

question: The Sunderban delta is the home of which of the following animal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Royal Bengal Tiger.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sundarbans delta, located at the mouth of the Ganga-Brahmaputra river system on the border of India (West Bengal) and Bangladesh, is home to the Royal Bengal Tiger. (सुंदरबन डेल्टा — रॉयल बंगाल टाइगर)

 

• It is the largest mangrove forest in the world and hosts a unique population of tigers specially adapted to a mangrove/aquatic habitat, known for their swimming ability.

 

• The Sundarbans National Park (India) is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a designated Tiger Reserve under Project Tiger, as well as a Biosphere Reserve and a Ramsar wetland site.

 

• The Sundarbans is formed by the confluence of the Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Meghna rivers and is criss-crossed by numerous tidal creeks and channels.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sundarbans is also home to other species such as saltwater crocodiles, Gangetic dolphins, and various bird species.

 

• Project Tiger was launched in 1973 to conserve the tiger population in India; the Sundarbans Tiger Reserve was established in 1973 as well.

 

NOTE

 

• Asiatic Cheetah (Option 1): Historically found in India but declared extinct in the country in 1952; not native to Sundarbans (African cheetahs have since been reintroduced at Kuno, Madhya Pradesh, not Sundarbans).

 

• Asiatic Lions (Option 2): Found only in the Gir Forest National Park, Gujarat, not in the Sundarbans.

 

• Black Panther (Option 4): A melanistic form of leopard, more commonly associated with dense forest regions like the Western Ghats (e.g., Kabini), not specifically iconic to the Sundarbans.
